          PSG 4-2 Barcelona Stats: Late Vitinha and Fabián Strikes End Barça's Perfect Start to Season
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Barcelona's winning start to the season is over after defeat in a Champions League thriller. Look back on the action with our PSG vs Barcelona stats page.
Vítinha and Fabián Ruiz struck in the last 10 minutes at the Parc des Princes to clinch Paris Saint-Germain a 4-2 win and end Barcelona’s perfect start to the season.
Both sides were guilty of wasting chances on Tuesday, but Désiré Doué gave PSG a half-time lead that Xavi Espart cancelled out early in the second half.
After Lamine Yamal then levelled after Lucas Hernández had put the reigning champions back in front, Vitinha and Fabian both scored late on to settle a Champions League thriller.

PSG almost got off to a dream start as Pedri was caught in possession and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Ousmane Dembélé latched onto the rebound and blazed wide of the empty net, but the offside flag spared his blushes.
Ferran Torres – an early replacement after Dembélé pulled up holding his hamstring – was played in behind Barcelona's defence, but Joan García was equal to his former teammate's scuffed volley.
And García's inspired form continued as he again denied Ferran from point-blank range before getting back to his feet to push away Fabián's bouncing volley.
The breakthrough came in the 38th minute, as João Neves cut out Yamal's dinked pass from defence, and Doué skipped away from his marker to curl past García.
Fermín López should have equalised a few moments later, but Matvey Safonov stood his ground to block the chip when one-on-one.
PSG started the second half on top as well, with Doué picking out the unmarked Achraf Hakimi, who could only aim his first-time effort at García.
Barcelona punished their hosts' profligacy in the 55th minute as a lovely flowing team move resulted in Fermín sliding in Espart to drill past Safonov.
But momentum was soon back with PSG. Ferran struck the post from close range, and from the next corner, Doué picked out Hernández to head past the helpless García.

Barcelona were not done yet. Yamal dragged them level with a piece of individual brilliance, rifling into the roof of the net from a tight angle after bursting past Warren Zaïre-Emery – who'd initially gifted him possession – with 11 minutes to go.

But Vitinha restored PSG’s advantage two minutes later; Hakimi's cross was only half cleared by Gerard Martín, and Vitinha smashed home from the edge of the box after chesting the ball down for himself.
Fabián made sure of all three points in the 86th minute, Hakimi's deflected cross finding the unmarked Spaniard for a tap-in.

If this fixture promised one thing, it was goals. The previous 15 European/Cup Champions League meetings between these sides saw a combined 57 goals scored, and this one arguably should have had even more than the six it produced.
PSG dominated the first half and got 10 of their 12 shots on target, the highest number of attempts on target Barcelona have faced before the break in the competition since at least 2003-04.
Despite being on the losing side, García proved a key part of Flick's side as he made 10 saves in total.
Flick's side have been the ones to beat in 2026-27, but their perfect record across all competitions has now ended – they had won all of their previous 11 games while scoring 50 goals.
The two teams combined for 40 shots (22 for PSG, 18 for Barça) and had 11 Opta-defined ‘big' chances between them (six for PSG, five for Barcelona).
